page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, the processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 236 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2165.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.43 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show relative limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth (36.7 GB/sec read, 25.67 GB/sec write) fall into lower performance tiers. Database operations and static web serving throughput remain moderate, with Passmark database operations scoring 2889.27 and web serving throughput reaching 7.73 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the D4ds_v6 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that do not demand extreme multi-threaded throughput or high memory bandwidth. The inclusion of local storage and dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable performance for applications such as moderate web serving, text processing, and light database operations. It is less suited for heavy software compilation, ray tracing, or memory-intensive caching layers due to weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth scaling.
